grounds.describes: the Wave B stage 1-6 blueprint (bond held to settlement, proportional W5 splits, proportional expire bounty, FavorNonRaiser, and stage 6's review window + timed release), read line by line 2026-08-30; RE-READ 2026-09-01 for two later changes this prose did not name and should have: (a) the L6(c) self-dealing guard (c5e8f8a, 2026-08-31) - modelled as the not(arbiterIsWorker) guard on resolveDispute and gated by the SELF-DEALING-GUARD-DELETED mutation; (b) resolve_dispute's arbiter_badge moving Bucket -> Proof and its return (Bucket,Bucket) -> Bucket (fa8c15e, 2026-09-01), because the Wave B badge is non-transferable. (b) needs NO model change, and the reason is checkable rather than asserted: mayResolve is a pure Actor predicate, no var in this model represents badge custody or movement, and the model's stated idealisation is 'holding the credential == passing the check'. Why this matters: `formal ground` rewrites only sha256 and verified, never this prose, so a stamp whose describes does not name the change reads as review that did not happen. NOT the deployed component: mainnet still runs the PULL-cutover build until the Wave B swap ceremony. RE-GROUNDED 2026-09-15 (P7-02, task 90, PR #654): lib.rs's ONLY change was one `pub mod nft_swap;` declaration (plus its doc comment) at the top of the file, wiring in a NEW, STANDALONE `NftSwap` blueprint that lives entirely in a sibling file (src/nft_swap.rs) and is never called from, or shares any struct/vault/method with, `guild_marketplace_escrow`. Confirmed by diff, not merely asserted: `git diff` against the pre-PR commit touches zero lines inside `mod guild_marketplace_escrow { ... }` — every inserted line is the six-line module declaration above the `// Config view + state types` banner. No state var, action, or invariant in this model is affected; re-grounded on that reading rather than on trust. NftSwap itself has no Quint model yet — tracked as deferred work (formal/nft_swap.qnt), not blocking this escrow re-ground.
grounds.note: PROJECT-STATE.md's 2026-07-31 'auto_resolve returns both buckets to the caller' entry describes the PRE-PULL blueprint and is superseded at PROJECT-STATE.md:5346. lib.rs won. If that file changes, this check FAILS until a human re-reads it and re-grounds.

Post-W5 the invariant is the forfeiture ledger (house + bounty == forfeited), because rulings now credit poster bond LEGITIMATELY and a total-take bound can no longer see this.

mutations.describes: submit reachable by a non-worker caller. NARROWED at 5b: submit_task no longer moves money (the bond is held to settlement), so what this now pins is the authority abstraction — an Anyone-reachable submit is an attacker-chosen evidence hash, griefing not theft. The bond-theft class itself is gated at SOURCE (test_submit_task_returns_nothing), because invConservation measurably cannot see it: the sums balance whoever is paid.

approve_and_release forgets the bond leg (5b regression): the task terminates Released with the bond still in its vault. CONSERVATION HOLDS under this bug — the money just sits — which is exactly why invNoBondLeftBehindAtSettlement exists as its own invariant.

mutations.describes: release_after_review_timeout (stage 6, W2) treats poster silence as a JUDGEMENT and hands the worker the insurance too. This is the faucet/dominance shape that kept auto-release refused for four months: a worker who submits and waits would collect MORE than honest approval pays, on a path they reach alone. The timeout must pay exactly what approve pays. (The other W2 hazard — firing BEFORE the window — is invariant-invisible here because it pays the same approve-equal amounts; the ledger test test_release_after_review_timeout_before_deadline_rejects gates it.)

mutations.describes: release_after_review_timeout (stage 6, W2) forgets the bond leg - the task terminates Released with the bond still in its vault. The SAME regression as BOND-STRANDED-AT-APPROVE against byte-identical code, and it had no mutation of its own until 2026-09-01: the harness's `replace` is non-global (formal.mjs: out.replace(op.from, op.to) unless op.all), so that entry only ever patched approveAndRelease and left the newer timed-release path ungated. Conservation HOLDS under this bug - the money simply sits - which is why invNoBondLeftBehindAtSettlement has to be its own invariant, and why a settlement path with no mutation of its own is a settlement path nothing checks.

mutations.describes: The L6(c) self-dealing guard (shipped 2026-08-30: resolve_dispute asserts the arbiter badge's assigned_account differs from task.worker_account) is stripped, AND the healthy instance's badge is re-assigned to the worker — both patches on the MAIN module, same shape as INSURANCE-FOLLOWS-DEFAULT's const flip. Both are needed: with the const false the deletion is invariant-invisible (vacuous), and with the guard present the const flip alone is refused at the ruling. A worker-arbiter then rules for themself — reward, insurance remainder, whole bond (W5 follows their own ruling) AND the fee, strictly more than honest delivery pays. Replaces CONFLICTED-ARBITER on the worker side. ⚠️ NOT a twin mutation deliberately: the harness runs twin mutations UNPATCHED (runTwin ignores apply), which is exactly how the first version of this entry reported NOT DETECTED against an intact guard.

mutations.describes: The side L6(c) leaves OPEN BY DESIGN: an arbiter badge assigned to the POSTER's account still rules (poster is a caller-supplied payout destination, not an identity — a poster-side check would be decoy-defeatable and read as a defence without being one). No patch: the unmodified model must produce this counterexample, or it has stopped representing the exposure the honesty copy states. The arbiter-poster can rule in a dispute they funded; they cannot STEAL (settlement credits only pinned accounts).
